clue.text: Female takeover for the flower show

blocks.note: Rose is a woman's name
read as 'take over': in cricket a bowler takes an over when sending down six deliveries

explanation.surface: A woman seizes control of the running of the local flower show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takeover' splits into 'take over': an over is a cricket term for a set of six balls delivered by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose bowl is a wide glass or silver vessel used to display cut blooms, so it puts flowers on show.

clue.text: A mother and father figure

blocks.note: taken as written
a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
joins the wordplay to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone who acts as both mother and father to a child.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'mother and father' but 'mother' belongs to the wordplay and 'father figure' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man is the forefather of all humanity, the ultimate patriarch.

clue.text: Lodge among native Indians

blocks.note: surface reading: a branch of a club or fraternal society among Native Americans
setter's reading: a dwelling, the kind of hut or tent used by some Native American peoples

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lodge' suggests a Masonic-style society; here it is a physical shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A wigwam is a domed hut of poles and bark or hides traditionally built by Native American peoples.

clue.text: Cup of tea left to go cold

blocks.note: cha is informal British for tea
L is the abbreviation for left
ice is what water becomes when it goes cold enough

explanation.surface: A cup of tea abandoned until it has cooled.
explanation.walkthrough: The published grid reads CHALLCE, a typo in an unchecked square: the wordplay and definition both give CHALICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalice is a large ornate drinking goblet, especially the one used for wine at Communion.

clue.text: Where the cat sat in the dog-house

blocks.note: first meaning: the classic first-reader sentence 'the cat sat ...'
second meaning: in trouble, facing a reprimand, as an employee summoned to the boss's mat

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the carpet' and this phrase both mean called up for a telling-off; the dog-house is the same disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase completes the nursery reading sentence and is also an idiom for being in disgrace and due a scolding.

clue.text: Like gremlins, be mischievous

indicators.note: letters that behave mischievously refuse to stay in their proper places

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to act like gremlins and cause playful trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean similar to or having the appearance of something else, as in 'like a bird'.

clue.text: Guard is fed up to death

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word fed is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
death is the end of life

explanation.surface: A sentry who is sick to death of the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up to death' looks like one idiom for being bored; it splits into three working parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To protect something from attack is to keep it safe, the verb sense of keeping watch over it.

clue.text: One that Midas got off the hook?

definitions.text: One that Midas got off the hook?

blocks.clueFragment: One that Midas got off the hook?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone the king rescued from trouble
setter's reading: a catch landed by the king whose touch turned everything to precious metal

explanation.walkthrough: King Midas turned all he touched to gold, so any fish he unhooked would become a golden one.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange carp kept in bowls and ponds is a fish, and one touched by Midas would literally be made of gold.

clue.text: It leaves refined niceties for female members of the family

indicators.note: something that leaves is taken away, so those letters depart from the longer word
refined suggests material processed and reworked, so the letters left are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written; these letters are removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone abandons polite social graces in favour of the women in the family.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I and T from NICETIES to leave NICEES, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is the daughter of one's brother or sister, so nieces are female relatives.

clue.text: Wide smile gives support

blocks.note: first meaning: a broad radiant grin
second meaning: a horizontal timber or girder holding up a structure

explanation.surface: A broad grin offers encouragement to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a broad happy grin and a long rigid bar that bears load in a building.

clue.text: Rich and of high standing?

blocks.note: first meaning: wealthy, comfortably off
second meaning, taken literally: standing tall on good high heels

explanation.walkthrough: 'High standing' sounds like social status; the question mark points to a literal reading about shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for wealthy comes from having well-made shoes, and taken literally it describes someone raised up on heels.

clue.text: Cannon ball?

blocks.note: first meaning: a rapid-firing automatic anti-aircraft gun named for its sound
second meaning: a fluffy ball of wool decorating a hat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cannon ball' reads as one thing, a projectile, but the two words are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a quick-firing naval gun and a woolly tuft used on bobble hats and by cheerleaders.

clue.text: He has no scruples about impoverishing those that stand by him

definitions.text: He has no scruples about impoverishing those that stand by him

blocks.clueFragment: He has no scruples about impoverishing those that stand by him
blocks.note: surface reading: someone who ruins loyal friends who support him
setter's reading: people literally standing next to him in a crowd, whose wallets he lifts

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand by' suggests loyalty; it means physical nearness, the people a thief can reach.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickpocket steals money and valuables from the clothing of people close by in crowds.

clue.text: They may support you when you retire in the country

definitions.text: They may support you when you retire in the country

blocks.clueFragment: They may support you when you retire in the country
blocks.note: surface reading: pensions or friends that sustain someone after moving to rural life
setter's reading: go to sleep outdoors while camping

explanation.walkthrough: 'Retire' means stop working in the surface but go to bed in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Folding portable cots carried on camping trips hold a sleeper off the ground in a tent.

clue.text: Identify unpleasant smell - but this won't cure anything

blocks.note: to place someone is to recognise who they are
BO stands for body odour

explanation.surface: Someone traces a bad smell and notes that the remedy is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill with no active ingredient is given for its psychological effect, not any medical action.

clue.text: Primate, one born during the last US President's time in office?

definitions.text: one born during the last US President's time in office?

blocks.note: first meaning: a small nocturnal African primate also called a galago

blocks.clueFragment: one born during the last US President's time in office?
blocks.note: second meaning: a child born in the Bush years, as with baby boomers

explanation.walkthrough: When this was published the most recent US President was George Bush, so a child of his term is named after him, as with 'baby boomers'.
explanation.definitionFit: The galago of African forests has this common name, and the phrase also fits a child of the Bush presidency.

clue.text: Occasionally imitates assembly after Head had left

indicators.note: once the head has gone, the opening letter of the word is missing
an assembly puts parts together in a new arrangement, so the letters are rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written; its first letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A school assembly where pupils sometimes mimic the head teacher once they have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first letter of IMITATES leaves MITATES for rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means now and then, from time to time, exactly the sense of the adverb.

clue.text: A compulsory turnout

blocks.note: surface reading: an event people are obliged to attend, a mandatory showing
setter's reading: being turned out of one's home by force

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnout' suggests attendance numbers; split it as 'turn out', to throw someone out.
explanation.definitionFit: Legally removing a tenant from a property is a forced expulsion from their home.

clue.text: Further progress

blocks.note: first meaning: to promote or help forward a cause
second meaning: forward movement or development

explanation.walkthrough: 'Further progress' reads as more headway; the two words are separate definitions, the first a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for promoting a cause and a noun or verb for forward movement.

clue.text: After drink, sat and thought

blocks.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
a model sat, or posed, for a portrait

explanation.surface: Someone has a drink, then sits down and reflects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After drink' tells you the drink comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean believed or assumed, as in 'I supposed you were away'.

clue.text: Dotty pair from Dôsseldorf

blocks.note: surface reading: an eccentric couple from the German city
setter's reading: two dots placed over a vowel, as in the city's own name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' means crazy in the surface but literally two dots here. The source text shows ô where the German name has ü.
explanation.definitionFit: The German diacritic of two dots over a vowel marks a changed vowel sound, as in Düsseldorf.

clue.text: Important person gives an extensive lecture

blocks.note: big means large or extensive
to wig is old British slang for to scold, so a wigging is a lecture

explanation.surface: A dignitary delivers a long talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a VIP, from the large wigs once worn by judges and grandees.

clue.text: A scoundrel not worth bidding for

blocks.note: first meaning: a dishonest or worthless person
second meaning, literally: a poor item at an auction

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a rogue, and read literally it is an auction item of poor quality.

clue.text: Note deficiency: get the governors to provide school equipment

blocks.note: B is a musical note
a lack is a shortage
a school's governing body is its board

explanation.surface: A memo about shortfalls asks the school governors to supply equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark writing surface for chalk is the classic fixture at the front of a classroom.

clue.text: Book some variety turns

blocks.note: first meaning: the ... of the Apostles in the New Testament
second meaning: performances in a variety show

explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb meaning to hire performers, but it is a noun naming a Bible book.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth New Testament book has this short title, and stage turns in a variety show are also called this.

clue.text: Port area

blocks.note: first meaning: the ancient harbour city in northern Israel
second meaning: a unit of land measuring 4,840 square yards

explanation.definitionFit: The Israeli harbour town shares its spelling with the imperial land-measurement unit.

clue.text: Pubs re-built providing choice

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a different shape

blocks.note: taken as written
the first part of the hyphenated word, used as letters

explanation.surface: Renovated pubs give drinkers more options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Re-built' does double duty: its first two letters join the fodder and the word as a whole signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, choice means of excellent quality, as in 'choice cuts of meat'.

clue.text: Young stallholder

blocks.note: surface reading: a youngster running a market stall
setter's reading: someone who occupies the choir stalls in a church

explanation.walkthrough: Choir stalls are the rows of seats in a church chancel where singers sit.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy who sings treble in a church choir sits in the chancel stalls during services.
